title: One-Step RT-ddPCR for Detection of SARS-CoV-2 and Bovine Coronavirus in Wastewater
author: Stephanie Loeb
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.br96m99e
materials: Sterilize workspace and equipment: UV pipettes, tube racks and molecular grade water, bleach bench and ice buckets (let sit ~ 10 min), turn on PCR hood UV light, wipe bench and ice buckets with 70% EtOH.

Gather reagents and thaw all components on ice for at least 00:15:00 : One Step RT-ddPCR Advanced Kit for Probes (stored in -20 °C ) Supermix Reverse transcriptase (RT) 300 mM dithiothreitol (DTT) solution Duplex assay mix of primers and probes (pre-prepared and stored at 4 °C ) One-Step RT-ddPCR Advanced Kit for Probes Bio-Rad Laboratories Catalog #186-4021

Gather autoDG materials and load them: DG32 cartridges (required: one green strip per column, check directionality, will turn green when seated) AutoDG pipet tips in racks (required: two columns of pipets or sample column) Check the level of the AutoDG oil for probes Remove the cooling black accessory from the freezer and place in the droplet plate location Empty droplet plate (new ddPCR plate into which the generated droplets will be dispensed) loaded into the cooling block
Within 5 minutes of it finishing droplet generation, remove the droplet containing plate from the cold block and seal in the plate sealer. Transfer to the thermocycler.

The plate can be transferred to the droplet reader immediately or left at 4 °C on the thermal cycler overnight and run on the droplet reader in the morning. While the thermocycler is running, prepare the droplet reader program as described below. Leaving the plate on the droplet reader overnight may improve droplet separation and plate reading.
Open QuantaSoft software (NOT QuantaSoft Analysis Pro).

steps.title: Prepare Assay Mixes
steps.instruction: Prepare 4X assay mixes for the targets and store at -20°C (or 4°C for up to 2 weeks if used frequently).

substeps.instruction: Resuspend lyophilized primers and probes to 100 µM in molecular grade TE buffer (e.g., add 348 µL TE to 34.8 nmol).
For SARS-CoV-2 4X mix (1 mL): Combine 36 µL each of N1-F, N1-R, N2-F, and N2-R; 10 µL N1-P-FAM; 10 µL N2-P-HEX; and 836 µL molecular grade water in a 2 mL LoBind epi-tube.

For BCoV-PMMoV 4X mix (1 mL): Combine 36 µL each of BCoV-F, BCoV-R, PMMoV-F, and PMMoV-R; 10 µL BCoV-P-FAM; 16 µL PMMoV-P-HEX; and molecular grade water to reach a final volume of 1 mL in a 2 mL LoBind epi-tube.

steps.title: Prepare Workspace and Reagents
steps.instruction: Clean the bench and organize reagents to prevent contamination and maintain temperature.

substeps.instruction: Wipe surfaces and equipment with 10% bleach, air dry for 10 min, and wipe with 70% ethanol.
Turn on the plate sealer (ensure block is not in machine).
Prepare a small bucket of ice for PCR reagents and a large bucket for samples.

steps.title: Prepare Sample Dilutions
steps.instruction: Prepare sample dilutions using molecular grade water (MGW) according to the worksheet.

substeps.instruction: Set up tubes with 27 µL of MGW.
Retrieve samples from -80°C freezer (use fresh aliquots; limit to one freeze/thaw cycle).
Vortex each tube for homogeneity and briefly spin down.
For SARS-CoV-2: Add 3 µL of sample to 27 µL MGW for a 1:10 dilution. Vortex and spin down.
For BCoV/PMMoV: Perform 1:10 dilution, then continue to dilute to 1:100 and 1:1000. Vortex and spin down.

steps.title: Prepare Reaction Master Mix
steps.instruction: Prepare the reaction mix in a PCR hood based on the target assay.

substeps.instruction: For both assays, use the following components per reaction: 5.5 µL Supermix (4X), 2.2 µL RT (10X), 1.1 µL DTT (300mM), 5.5 µL Duplex Assay Mix (4X), and 2.2 µL molecular-grade H2O.
Dispense 16.5 µL of the mix into each reaction well.
Fill any empty wells in a column with 22 µL of ddPCR Buffer Control for Probes (catalog #1863052) diluted 1:1 with water.

steps.title: Load Plate and Seal
steps.instruction: Add templates to the plate and seal for droplet generation.

substeps.instruction: Load 5.5 µL of template per well according to the worksheet (e.g., for SARS-CoV-2: 3 wells undiluted and 3 wells 1:10; for BCoV/PMMoV: 2 wells 1:10 and 2 wells 1:1000).
Include NTCs (molecular grade water) and positive controls (Clinical RNA for SARS-CoV-2; 10^6 cp/mL BCoV vaccine for BCoV; synthetic ultramer for PMMoV).
Seal the plate with a heat seal cover using the plate sealer.
Vortex the plate for 30 seconds, then centrifuge at 1000 rpm for 1 minute.

steps.title: Generate Droplets
steps.instruction: Use the automated droplet generator (AutoDG) to create droplets.

substeps.instruction: Ensure trash is empty and a cooling block has been stored at -20°C for at least 2 hours.
Load the sealed plate into the AutoDG; confirm the indicator light is green.
Configure the sample plate on the interface, select active columns, enter plate name, and run.

steps.title: Perform Thermocycling
steps.instruction: Run the RT-ddPCR cycling protocol on the thermocycler.

substeps.instruction: Apply the following common phases: RT (50°C, 60 min, 1 cycle), Enzyme Activation (95°C, 10 min, 1 cycle), Denature (94°C, 30 sec, 40 cycles), Enzyme deactivation (98°C, 10 min, 1 cycle), Droplet Stabilization (4°C, 30 min, 1 cycle), and Hold (4°C, infinite).
Set the Anneal/Extension temperature: 55°C for 1 min (N1/N2) or 60°C for 1 min (BCoV/PMMoV).

steps.title: Read Droplets and Analyze Data
steps.instruction: Read the processed plate in the droplet reader and export the data.

substeps.instruction: Prime the droplet reader via the Instrument Routines panel.
Transfer the plate from the thermocycler to the droplet reader holder.
Set the Supermix parameter to 'One-Step RT-ddPCR kit for probes' (critical step).
Load a template from a previous plate of the same assay to ensure correct dye/absorbance parameters, then update sample names.
Run the reader (approx. 90 seconds per well).
Open QuantaSoft Analysis Pro, browse to the plate folder, and open the .ddpcr file.
Save the data to a USB key as a .ddpcr file.
